newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: BASS SEES EXERCISING OPTION IN CZECH BREWER PP.
newsitem.headline: BASS SEES EXERCISING OPTION IN CZECH BREWER PP.

text.p: British brewer Bass Plc said on Monday it would probably exercise an option in Czech brewery Prazske Pivovary a.s. at the start of November to give it a majority stake in the Prague-based brewer.

"We have 46 percent in Prazske Pivovary now and we also have a five percent option exercisable at the beginning of November...I think we'll exercise that option," said Mervyn Childs, Bass country manager for the Czech Republic.
Prazske Pivovary (PP) is one of the top four brewing groups in the Czech Republic producing some of the country's most popular brands such as Staropramen, Mestan and Branik.
In 1993 Bass took a 34 percent stake in PP for nine million pounds and has gradually increased its stake.
Childs said that Bass foresaw a consolidation in the Czech brewing industry with many smaller brewers being swallowed up and three major groups emerging.
In July Bass took a 20 percent stake in another of the country's top brewing groups, north-Moravia based Radegast a.s. .
Childs said Bass was talking to other major shareholders in Radegast -- IPB Bank a.s which has 34 percent and KIS a.s. which has around 30 percent - about increasing its stake.
"But we've made no secret of saying we're talking to other shareholders in Radegast. We have 20 percent but would like to increase that shareholding," Childs told Reuters.
"I would like to think there has been some movement (on this) by the end of the year," he added.
Childs said that if plans to take a bigger share in Radegast failed, Bass would look elsewhere in the Czech brewing industry to strengthen its position.
The British Brewer also has large stakes in two small regional Czech breweries.
